regressions.source: Governor.execute/queue/cancel -> state(), quorum(), timelock.isOperationDone/isOperationPending/getMinDelay/cancel, emit ProposalExecuted/ProposalCanceled; propose -> getVotes; hashProposal = keccak256(abi.encode(...))
regressions.issue: After mem[64] is set to the pointer left by the abi.encode loop of hashProposal, a read of mem[64] is neither that value nor above a floor, so writes through it may alias everything: Governor string reverts become raw (decoded 82 -> 58), the timelock/token calls lose names and args (P2 15 -> 38 lines), the events take memory slices, and mapping reads lose their keys (29 stor[sha3(mem[0 len 64])], P4 23 -> 42). The old text resolved all of these.
regressions.rule: After mem[64] = x, a read of mem[64] is x until the next write to mem[64], even for a loop-carried x; a pointer that starts at or above a constant floor and only grows keeps the floor, so writes at mem[64] + k (k >= 0) cannot alias [0, 64) or memory below the floor.

regressions.source: Governor.sol execute: require(status == Succeeded || status == Queued, 'Governor: proposal not successful')
regressions.issue: A guard revert became an else arm at the end, nesting the body under the opposite test.
regressions.rule: Print a branch that ends every path (revert) first, as a guard clause, and keep the rest at the outer level.

improvements: P6 fixed. P3 fixed in the 7 onlyGovernance functions. castVoteBySig and castVoteWithReasonAndParamsBySig: getPastTotalSupply, getPastVotes, isOperationDone, isOperationPending named; ECDSA and Bravo reverts decoded; VoteCast/VoteCastWithParams decoded; return weight. In castVoteBySig the empty reason/params are now known, so the dead VoteCastWithParams arm and its zero-length copy loops are gone (407 -> 140 lines). castVote shares the 'vote not currently active' revert tail and loses a meaningless require; the other castVote* events are decoded.
notes: Diff 4817 lines, reviewed by structure: per-function effects and control-statement diffs for all 22 changed functions, with execute, hashProposal, castVote, castVoteBySig and setVotingDelay read in detail. The regression is one cause (lost free-pointer value/floor after a loop) seen in 7 functions; queue also prints a call as timelock.mem[mem[64] len 4].
summary: Medium regression: in execute, queue, cancel, propose and hashProposal the free pointer is lost after the hashing loop, so Governor reverts, timelock/token calls, events and mapping keys that the old text decoded are raw again (P2 15 -> 38, P4 23 -> 42). Gains: rotated popFront loops fixed, castVote*BySig fully decoded and much shorter.
